revenue_estimate.note: No observed price — revenue left unestimated rather than inferred from search volume.

positive_signals: 7 small vendors selling, none funded — demand proven, room to differentiate
negative_signals: 5 Product Hunt launches in this space
vendors own the buyer-intent results page — paid may be the only channel

claude_analysis.tam_assessment: Niche research-tooling market: the only real evidence is a handful of EEG hardware vendors (Mentalab, mBrainTrain, Neurosity, Bitbrain, MindRove) that sell their own synchronization features, a declining 'EEG synchronization' Google Trends curve (avg 44, down), zero Hacker News posts, and Reddit/Product Hunt hits that are mostly unrelated (password managers, file transfer), so the buyer pool looks limited to academic and clinical EEG, hyperscanning, and multimodal labs, which I estimate at around 10,000 worldwide.
claude_analysis.pricing_assessment: The data contains no observed competitor price, so ~$1,000/yr per lab is an assumption based on typical research-software and sync-hardware budgets, and willingness to pay is limited because the free, open-source Lab Streaming Layer (LSL, referenced in the Mentalab snippet) is the default method and vendors bundle sync with their own devices.
claude_analysis.legal_reasoning: The regulatory probe returned 0 restriction hits and 0 government sources, so no licensing or standing rules surfaced for selling research sync software, though a clinical/diagnostic positioning could trigger medical-device rules that were not probed.
key_risks: The free open-source Lab Streaming Layer is already the default method for timestamp alignment
EEG hardware vendors (Mentalab Hypersync, mBrainTrain) bundle synchronization with their own devices, which limits the market for third-party tools
Search results are owned by vendors (50% vendor share) and academic buyers have slow grant-driven purchasing, which raises acquisition cost
key_opportunities: Cross-vendor sync for labs that mix devices from different manufacturers is not handled by single-vendor bundles
Growth in hyperscanning and multimodal (EEG + eye-tracking/motion/fNIRS) research raises the need for validated sub-millisecond sync
None of the incumbents found shows any recorded funding, so no well-capitalized player owns the cross-device niche
claude_analysis.value_reasoning: 10,000 potential labs × $1,000/yr ≈ $10M total addressable annual revenue.
claude_analysis.probability_reasoning: Competition is 'contested', so no ceiling applies, but the free LSL standard and vendor-bundled sync keep realistic penetration of an already small niche at around 1% or less, which puts this in the moonshot tier.
